articles.title: Pune police and Military Intelligence detain three Bangladeshi nationals over illegal stay
articles.content: ANI Photo | Pune police and Military Intelligence detain three Bangladeshi nationals over illegal stay Pune City Police’s Special Branch, in collaboration with Military Intelligence, detained three Bangladeshi nationals allegedly residing illegally in the city on August 27, officials said. The individuals have been identified as Sonia Akther, Motiar Gaji and Sonia Moti Pan. Acting on specific intelligence input, a joint operation was conducted around 3 pm resulting in their detention. Add TNM on Google During preliminary questioning and verification, authorities discovered the trio were residing in India without valid documentation. Detention orders are being issued, and they will remain in custody pending further legal proceedings and deportation formalities. The operation is part of intensified surveillance by intelligence and law enforcement agencies in Pune aimed at identifying persons without valid documents and uncovering networks involved in illegal entry or residence. ADVERTISEMENT Separately, Pune City Police announced a complete ban on plasma sound systems and pressure mids ahead of the upcoming festive season, including Dahi Handi and Ganeshotsav. Violators will face seizure of sound equipment and legal action under the Noise Pollution Rules. Pune City Police Commissioner Amitesh Kumar reported that six high-decibel sound setups were seized during recent Eid processions as enforcement against noise pollution was intensified ahead of the festivals. The police are discussing proposals with political leaders, dahi handi organisers and Ganesh mandals to limit procession sound systems to a maximum of “4 Base + 4 Top” speakers. While reasonable limits on sound usage are being considered, there will be zero tolerance for unapproved high-decibel equipment generating uncontrolled noise. ADVERTISEMENT “A total of 100% mutual consensus has been reached that any kind of plasma and pressure mid, through which uncontrolled noise is generated, has been completely banned,” Mr Kumar said. “All Ganesh mandals have assured us of voluntary compliance. If there is any violation of this anywhere, legal action under the Noise Pollution Rules will be taken, and the sound system will be seized.” Written by TNM (With ANI Inputs) This story is written by TNM Bureau with inputs from ANI.
